item.title: Spain's former central bank head chosen as next European Central Bank president
item.description:
Spain's former central bank head chosen as next European Central Bank president
Eurozone leaders have chosen a new president of the European Central BankByDAVID MCHUGH Associated Press and SAM MCNEIL Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 10:46 AM
Share
BRUSSELS -- European leaders have chosen the former head of Spain’s central bank, Pablo Hernández de Cos, to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank as the key EU institution confronts inflation driven by the war in Iran and worries about high government debt and borrowing costs in Europe.
Leaders from the 21 European member countries that use the euro also filled two other top posts at the ECB, which decides borrowing costs for the 359 million people in the eurozone.
European Council President António Costa said on X that the body agreed on the three appointments at a summit in Brussels.
De Cos’ nomination still must pass review by the European Parliament and the ECB’s governing council, but those steps are formalities.
The appointment puts an experienced central banker with a reputation for backing lower interest rates and monetary stimulus in charge at a time when several European governments are struggling with heavy debt loads and rising borrowing costs. De Cos, 55, served on the ECB rate-setting council from 2018 to 2024 through his post as head of the Spanish central bank.
A review of his speeches by Commerzbank analysts “suggests that de Cos is among the monetary policy doves,” or policymakers who lean toward lower rates to support growth.
De Cos won out over another main contender for the post, former Netherlands central bank head Klaas Knot, who was regarded as a hawk, or someone who favors higher rates to ward off inflation.

item.title: Rescuers battle tough conditions in flooded Indonesian mine
item.description:
Rescuers battle tough conditions in flooded Indonesian mine
Rescuers are battling high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain while searching for miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mineByNINIEK KARMINI Associated PressNovember 25, 2026, 10:43 PM
JAKARTA, Indonesia -- Rescuers battled high water, darkness and slippery, narrow terrain Thursday searching for 10 miners believed trapped by flooding in an illegal gold mine where 16 bodies have been recovered.
The miners were digging for grains of gold late Monday when heavy rain caused the Ciseureuh River to overflow into a mine shaft in the Bogor regency of West Java province. Several people escaped from one section of the excavation before floodwaters filled the shaft, estimated to be about 100 meters (330 feet) deep, in a mountainous area south of the capital, Jakarta.
Authorities said they were not immediately notified because the miners were operating illegally, and local miners and residents initially tried to pump water from the site themselves before the situation became unmanageable.
Police first received reports of trapped miners about 16 hours after the flooding occurred, and nearby state-owned mining company PT Antam forwarded a formal report to the Jakarta Search and Rescue Agency shortly after midnight Wednesday, triggering a full-scale rescue operation.
The search and rescue team used submersible water pumps to suck water from the hole and tried to close off openings where groundwater seeped in.
West Java police spokesperson Hendra Rochmawan said authorities believe at least 10 miners remain trapped as rescuers retrieved 16 bodies by Thursday.

item.title: Schizophrenic man found guilty of attempted murders of 14, including 10 on train
item.description:
Schizophrenic man found guilty of attempted murders of 14, including 10 on train
A schizophrenic man has been found guilty of the attempted murders of 14 people over three separate incidents over a 24-hour period that culminated with the stabbing of 10 people on a high-speed London-bound trainByPAN PYLAS Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 12:53 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LONDON -- A schizophrenic man was found guilty Thursday of the attempted murders of 14 people over three separate incidents over a 24-hour period that culminated with the stabbing of 10 people on a high-speed London-bound train.
Anthony Williams, 33, had admitted carrying out the attacks but denied that he intended to kill. His trial at Cambridge Crown Court was told that he was suffering from an acute psychosis at the time as a result of his schizophrenia.
But he was found guilty of all 14 counts of attempted murder by a jury after 16 hours and 52 minutes of deliberations. Most of the verdicts were unanimous.
Williams started his stabbing rampage on the evening of Oct. 31, 2025, when he knifed a boy and attempted to stab two men in the town of Peterborough, around 75 miles north of the capital.
He then traveled to London, where he stabbed a boy on a metro train in the early hours of Nov. 1, before returning to Peterborough and spending much of the day at home.
That evening, he boarded an LNER train service and stabbed nine passengers and a member of the onboard staff during his five-minute attack.
All survived their injuries.
One of those stabbed, Samir Zitouni, a member of the crew, had life-threatening injuries, having received stab wounds including three to the back while he was trying to fend off Williams with a frying pan. He suffered “catastrophic blood loss” and required four blood transfusions.

item.title: Serbia sets presidential election for Dec. 27 after students won parliamentary vote
item.description:
Serbia sets presidential election for Dec. 27 after students won parliamentary vote
Serbia's Parliament speaker has set an early presidential election for December 27ByJOVANA GEC Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 6:57 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BELGRADE, Serbia -- BELGRADE, Serbia (AP) — Serbia 's Parliament speaker on Thursday set an early presidential election for Dec. 27, after former President Aleksandar Vucic resigned in September to pursue what turned out to be a failed bid to become prime minister.
The presidential vote will be held after a student movement defeated Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party in an early parliamentary ballot on Oct. 25.
Vucic and his party had ruled virtually unchallenged for 14 years. He had run for prime minister after serving two near-complete five-year terms as president, and was banned by law from seeking a third term.
“I hope we will have a tough choice between top candidates and their programs," Speaker Aleksandar Cupic said. “Building democratic institutions is the task for all of us.”
It was not immediately clear who the presidential candidates will be. Vucic has suggested that his SNS party could sit out the election.

item.title: US-backed Ebola quarantine center violated constitution, Kenyan court rules
item.description:
US-backed Ebola quarantine center violated constitution, Kenyan court rules
Kenya's government violated the constitution by allowing the construction of a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility without public participation, the High Court has ruledByEVELYNE MUSAMBI Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 7:16 AM
NAIROBI, Kenya -- Kenya’s government violated the Constitution by allowing the construction of a U.S.-backed Ebola quarantine facility without public participation, a senior court ruled on Thursday.
The 50-bed facility at a military base in Laikipia sparked deadly protests by residents who feared exposure to the virus and an outbreak that could overwhelm Kenya's fragile health system.
In May, the High Court had ordered construction of the facility to be halted pending the determination of a case filed by the Law Society of Kenya and constitutional watchdog Katiba Institute. The petitioners argued that Kenya’s fragile health system was ill-equipped to handle a potential Ebola outbreak.
Trump administration officials had said Americans exposed to Ebola abroad would be sent to the facility rather than flown home. The U.S. government planned to commit $13.5 million to Kenya’s Ebola preparedness efforts.
Justice Patricia Nyaundi on Thursday ordered the government to disclose all agreements with the U.S. within 45 days. She also barred further construction or operations at the facility.

item.title: Emirati curator Hoor Al Qasimi becomes first Arab woman to lead Venice Biennale art show
item.description:
Emirati curator Hoor Al Qasimi becomes first Arab woman to lead Venice Biennale art show
Hoor Al Qasimi has been named as the first Arab and seventh woman to lead the Venice Biennale contemporary art exhibition, set for 2028ByCOLLEEN BARRY Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 8:43 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
MILAN -- Emirati curator Hoor Al Qasimi was named Thursday as the first Arab and the seventh woman to lead the Venice Biennale contemporary art exhibition, scheduled for 2028.
Al Qasimi leads the Sharjah Art Foundation, which she founded in 2009 to promote contemporary art and foster cultural exchange in the emirate, and has run the Sharjah Biennial since 2003. She is the daughter of the emirate’s ruler and curated the UAE’s pavilion at Venice in 2015.
The influential contemporary art magazine ArtReview ranked her No. 1 on its 2024 Power 100 list of the contemporary art world’s most influential figures, highlighting her support for artists beyond the Western mainstream.
The curator’s role is to present an organizing theme for the 62nd International Art Exhibition and choose artists for the main curated show, which runs alongside national pavilions that often take cues from the curator’s vision.

item.title: Building collapse in Pakistan kills 4, with 17 still missing
item.description:
Building collapse in Pakistan kills 4, with 17 still missing
A six-story building under construction collapsed in Karachi on Wednesday, killing at least four peopleByThe Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 3:30 AM
KARACHI, Pakistan -- A six-story building under construction collapsed in Karachi on Wednesday, killing at least four people, police and rescue officials said Thursday as rescuers searched for 17 others believed trapped beneath the rubble.
Another 14 people with injuries have been pulled from the collapsed building in Karachi’s Baloch Colony neighborhood, local police official Ammar Awan said.
TV footage from the scene in Pakistan’s southern port city showed rescuers in orange uniforms and helmets standing on enormous slabs of collapsed concrete amid broken masonry and tangled construction supports. Rescue officials initially reported one death before recovering three more bodies overnight.
Nasrullah Abbasi, a government official, said families had reported 17 people missing since the building collapsed.

item.title: Hong Kong marks deadly fire anniversary with flowers and tears following gov warning
item.description:
Hong Kong marks deadly fire anniversary with flowers and tears following gov warning
Hong Kong residents are remembering the victims of the city's deadliest fire in decades by offering flowers and prayersByKANIS LEUNG Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 1:09 AM
HONG KONG -- Hong Kong residents on Thursday remembered the victims of the city's deadliest fire in decades by offering flowers and prayers. But the commemorations were closely watched by authorities, who had warned against any attempt to exploit the tragedy and stir trouble.
The blaze engulfed seven high-rise buildings in Wang Fuk Court on Nov. 26, 2025, killing 168 people and displacing thousands of others in a disaster unimaginable in the wealthy financial hub known for its safety and modernity.
A year on, many fire survivors were still grieving their losses as they adjusted to their temporary housing, arranged funerals for their loved ones, cleaned up their belongings retrieved from charred homes and decided on resettlement plans.
At a park near the apartment complex in Tai Po in the north of Hong Kong, a steady stream of residents laid flowers, snacks and toys in tribute. Some returned to gaze at their old homes. Others wept.
As more residents turned out, officers from the Civil Aid Service, a government agency, put many flowers into transparent plastic boxes and placed them behind the main flower-laying area, saying it was to make room. One person from the crowd shouted: “Please have some conscience.”
Former Wang Fuk Court resident Louis Chan felt it was disrespectful. Student Tim Yu, 19, took issue with the officers not answering the public's questions. “This is the thing that chills my heart most this winter,” he said.
Some picked up the flowers from the ground and moved them to another spot in the park. Flowers were also offered in other spots near the complex.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau’s military junta postpones elections until 2028, extending its rule by two years
item.description:
Guinea-Bissau’s military junta postpones elections until 2028, extending its rule by two years
Guinea-Bissau’s military government has postponed presidential and legislative elections until November 2028, extending its promised yearlong transition to civilian rule by roughly two yearsByASSANA SAMBU Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 12:53 PM
BISSAU, Guinea-Bissau -- The military government in Guinea-Bissau on Thursday postponed presidential and legislative elections until November 2028, extending its promised yearlong transition to civilian rule by roughly two years.
The decision came on the first anniversary of the coup. The military seized power on Nov. 26, 2025, three days after general elections, ousting President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and interrupting the electoral process before official results were announced. Embaló and opposition candidate Fernando Dias had both claimed victory.
New presidential elections had initially been scheduled for next month. Prime Minister Ilídio Vieira Té said last month that conditions were not in place for December elections but gave no alternative date.
Transitional President Gen. Horta Inta-a set the elections for Nov. 26, 2028, in a decree published Thursday by the presidency and seen by The Associated Press.
The decree said the technical, material and financial conditions needed to organize credible elections were not in place. Holding the vote without meeting legal and operational requirements could undermine its transparency, inclusiveness and credibility, as well as public confidence in the process, it said.

item.title: Sierra Leone sees steep decline in maternal mortality, but barriers to care persist
item.description:
Sierra Leone sees steep decline in maternal mortality, but barriers to care persist
Fatmata Kamara's experience in Sierra Leone highlights both progress and challenges in maternal healthcareByKEMO CHAM Associated Press and MARK BANCHEREAU Associated PressNovember 26, 2026, 12:04 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
FREETOWN, Sierra Leone -- During her first two pregnancies, Fatmata Kamara could not afford ultrasound scans at a hospital in Sierra Leone’s capital, Freetown. By her third, she was receiving scans and medication and spending less time waiting to see a doctor.
But care that the government says should be free still came at a cost. Kamara said she spent 1,000 leones ($44) on medication and unofficial fees during her latest pregnancy.
“This pregnancy was different because of the attention I received at the hospital,” said the 28-year-old trader who gave birth to her third child last month at a health center in Freetown’s Mabela neighborhood. The services were "far better" than in the past, she said.
Kamara’s experience reflects both the progress and persistent challenges in Sierra Leone, which has recorded one of Africa's steepest declines in maternal mortality.
The country's maternal mortality ratio fell by nearly 80% from more than 1,600 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2000 to 354 in 2023, according to the latest available U.N. estimates.
The World Health Organization attributes Sierra Leone’s declining maternal mortality rate partly to expanded health services, the introduction of free maternal health care in 2010 and the training of more skilled birth attendants.
Despite the progress, unofficial fees, mistrust and poor infrastructure continue to hinder access to maternity care. A 300-day government campaign is also underway to advance the fight against preventable maternal and child deaths. ___
